facts.text: Physical tests needed to build and check a braking model are real-machine measurements used to calibrate model parameters and validate predictions on cases not used for tuning.
facts.quote: These are the measurements on a real machine that give a braking model its numbers (calibration) and then show whether its predictions hold on cases it has not seen (validation).

facts.text: Braking-model calibration tests measure parameters such as machine mass, brake engagement delay and achievable deceleration on gravel.
facts.quote: Calibration tests measure parameters: how heavy the machine is, how long the brakes take to bite, how hard they can decelerate it on gravel.

facts.text: Braking-model validation tests compare predictions with real measurements in situations not used for tuning; the booklet prohibits using the same stop for both tuning and claiming validation.
facts.quote: Validation tests then run situations the model was not tuned on and compare prediction with measurement. The booklet's rule: "never use the same stop to both tune and claim validation" [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet's braking-model physical test types include mass, geometry and load-state characterization at several payloads.
facts.quote: mass, geometry and load-state characterization at several payloads

facts.text: The booklet calls for brake-actuator identification on the automated path, using time-stamped command, pressure and deceleration measurements to identify dead time, rise time and release time.
facts.quote: brake-actuator identification (time-stamped command, pressure and deceleration to find dead time, rise time and release time, on the automated path)

facts.text: The booklet's braking-model physical test types include propulsion and retarder identification.
facts.quote: propulsion and retarder identification

facts.text: The booklet calls for straight-line stops at several speeds, payloads, brake temperatures, grades and surfaces, measuring stopping distance both from the collision-system command and from brake-force onset.
facts.quote: straight-line stops at several speeds, payloads, brake temperatures, grades and surfaces, measuring distance both from the collision-system command and from brake-force onset

facts.text: The booklet's braking-model physical test types include stability tests while braking during steering or articulation and on cross-slopes.
facts.quote: stability tests braking while steering or articulating and on cross-slopes

facts.text: The booklet's braking-model physical test types include crawler and soft-ground identification.
facts.quote: crawler and soft-ground identification

facts.text: The booklet's braking-model physical test types include hot-brake, downhill and repeated-stop tests.
facts.quote: hot-brake, downhill and repeated-stop tests

facts.text: The booklet's braking-model physical test types include hold and restart tests on grade.
facts.quote: hold and restart tests on grade

facts.text: The booklet's braking-model physical test types include end-to-end latency tests.
facts.quote: and end-to-end latency tests.

facts.text: No standard or study gives a number of physical tests needed to build and check a braking model, according to the booklet.
facts.quote: How many? No standard or study gives a number [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet's indicative physical-test matrix per machine family and brake architecture includes a latency sweep with at least 10 repetitions across oil temperatures.
facts.quote: an indicative matrix per machine family and brake architecture: a latency sweep with at least 10 repetitions across oil temperatures

facts.text: The booklet's indicative physical-test matrix per machine family and brake architecture includes stops at three speeds, two payloads, level and maximum design grade, with three repetitions each.
facts.quote: stops at three speeds, two payloads, level and maximum design grade, three repetitions each

facts.text: The booklet's indicative physical-test matrix per machine family and brake architecture includes one low-speed surface matrix covering hard, loose and wet surfaces.
facts.quote: one surface matrix (hard, loose, wet) at low speed

facts.text: For articulated machines, the booklet's indicative physical-test matrix includes stops at the articulation limit and on a side slope.
facts.quote: for articulated machines stops at the articulation limit and on a side slope

facts.text: The booklet estimates roughly 60 to 100 instrumented physical runs per machine family; completing these runs within the validation window is achievable only if families share instrumentation.
facts.quote: That is roughly 60 to 100 instrumented runs per family, "achievable in the window only if families share instrumentation" [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet's physical-test stopping rule is to add tests only where prediction intervals are too wide, residuals are systematically biased, or a case lies outside the validated domain.
facts.quote: Its stopping rule: add tests only where prediction intervals are too wide, residuals are systematically biased, or the case lies outside the validated domain.

facts.text: Prototype physical tests are intended for parameter identification and independent falsification, not for replaying every virtual scenario on the machine.
facts.quote: The purpose of the prototype tests is parameter identification and independent falsification, not replaying every virtual scenario on the machine [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet recommends pre-booking the prototype physical-test campaign for the first six weeks after hardware delivery.
facts.quote: The booklet recommends pre-booking this campaign for the first six weeks after hardware delivery

facts.text: The booklet recommends using existing machines before 2027 to learn the distributions of brake delay, grade response and load effects in advance.
facts.quote: using existing machines before 2027 to learn the distributions of brake delay, grade response and load effects in advance [Chapter 8].
